decisions.reason: A startup accelerator is far from the firm's core machinery business and brings no direct revenue, so a young firm with little slack is likely to cut it and move the resources to its core recycling plants.

The bio-based bitumen binder is a materials venture outside machinery and its results are uncertain, but its own dedicated page and its fit with the sustainability profile suggest management will give it more time before searching for other uses of the resources.
The infectious waste plant builds on the WASTX/MACS technology and a partnership with ERMAFA, which shares the cost and risk, so it is worth keeping while market feedback comes in.
The mobile recycling plant is the newest extension of the core WASTX line and is featured prominently, which makes it central to the firm's aspirations and unlikely to be dropped this early.
